segments.line: Here's the deal. Your brain has stopped sending the signal that says, sleep now.
You don't feel tired. Your eyes don't burn. You don't yawn.
But here's the catch nobody told you.
Feeling tired and needing sleep are two different things. Feeling sleepy is just the alarm.
It comes from a chemical called adenosine.
Every hour you're awake, more of it piles up in your brain, like sand in an hourglass.
Sleep is what tips the hourglass back over.
Your alarm is broken. But the clock is still ticking.
So you make one rule. If anything weird happens, anything at all, you tell Mo. Mo is your best friend, and the most honest person
you know. You even write it on a sticky note on your mirror. Tell Mo.
Mo thinks about it. 'Deal. But if you ever start talking to the fridge, I'm calling your mum'.
